newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica has 1.5mln "discouraged workers" - economist.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica has 1.5mln "discouraged workers" - economist.

text.p: South Africa is saddled with about 1.5 million "discouraged workers," one of the highest rates worldwide, and is not expected to find relief soon, Rand Afrikaans University economist Elsabe Loots said on Wednesday.

Addressing a National Productivity Institute conference, Loots defined "discouraged workers" as unemployed people younger than 30 years old who were not trained and skilled for the labour market and had lost hope of finding jobs.
She said the country's unemployment situation was deteriorating despite positive economic growth and a recovery phase in the business cycle.
Real economic growth on its own did not significantly contribute to the creation of new jobs because South Africa was experiencing a situation of "jobless economic growth."
"South Africa has approximately 1.5 million discouraged workers, which is one of the highest rates in the world," Loots said.
South Africa's labour market was characterised by high and inflexible wages, low productivity and high labour unit costs.
Loots said the country should move towards a higher growth path which implied faster employment-led growth.

"Labour-intensive sectors, which make the best use of abundant low-skilled labour, should be identified. In this regard, export industries and direct foreign investment could play a major role," she said.
South Africa's unemployment rate reached an estimated high of 33.8 percent last year.
While the formal sector had been able to absorb more than 80 percent of the labour force in the period preceding 1983, this figure declined to an estimated 53.2 percent last year, Loots said.
